A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StitchCUDA and provide readable methods, equations, results, figures and Appendices A-C. Retained content can be matched despite reflow and table renumbering; no material comparison gaps were found.

before.justification: V1 reports original KernelBench evaluations on H200 and RTX PRO 6000, rubric ablations, hacking analyses and an appendix case study.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds individual rubric-component ablations and a Claude-based framework evaluation.

M1.justification: The Planner/Coder/Verifier workflow, RAG integration, two atomic training skills, four rubric dimensions and reward formulation remain unchanged. The additional ablation variants and Coder comparator do not revise the proposed full method.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same modified KernelBench Levels 1-3 coverage. Added ablations use the existing H200 Level 3 setting. Benchmarks newly cited in Section 5.3 are discussed, not evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds StitchCUDA-C, identified as using Claude-4.6-Sonnet, to the RTX PRO 6000 comparison only. Existing comparators remain. The standalone row still says Claude-4-sonnet, so the prose's claimed model-matched Claude comparison is not clearly documented.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 introduces four controlled training variants, each omitting one rubric dimension while retaining the other three, evaluated on H200 Level 3. Existing experiments retain the 80/20 task split, task counts, 15-iteration budget and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's whole-rubric versus no-rubric ablation, v2 independently removes Anti-Hacking, CUDA Engineering, Operator Coverage and Skill Compliance in new Table 2. This substantially extends analysis of the central reward design by isolating each component's effects on correctness, speedup and hacking.

E5.justification: No confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests or repeated-run counts are added. Correctness checking across multiple random seeds is retained. The new ablation table presents fractional counts without explaining their aggregation or a statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds StitchCUDA-C results, including RTX PRO 6000 Level 3 correctness of 9/10 and 1.18x speedup. New Table 2 reports component-ablation outcomes, such as 5.7/10 correctness and 0.75x speedup without Anti-Hacking. Previously reported benchmark, hacking and appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The reward definitions, GRPO objective and Appendix A's mathematical explanation of zero-output degeneracy and its top-k modification are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about end-to-end generation, atomic-skill RL, reward-hacking mitigation and performance. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of individual rubric-component effects. New Section 5.3 qualifies applicability through limitations concerning hardware portability, agents' ability to use new GPU knowledge, and benchmarks' incomplete coverage of robustness, deployment and regression behavior.

D1.justification: V2 newly states that framework code is available and supplies a repository address after the introduction. Training hyperparameters, hardware, prompts, RAG construction and implementation examples otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5.3 adds discussion and citations of CUDABench, TritonBench, ComputeEval, CUDAHercules and CUDABeaver to contextualize benchmark limitations and future directions. Existing methodological positioning remains intact; Astra and QiMeng bibliography edits concern existing works.

P1.justification: V2 expands Section 4.2, adds Section 5.3 and acknowledgements, and updates author affiliations, the equal-contribution note and publication metadata. Most existing prose and the overall section organization are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the rubric-ablation table and a row and caption extension in Table 1. Figures 2-3 are enlarged without changing their content; Figure 4 and surrounding material reflow. Existing later tables are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The component ablations strengthen support for the rubric design, while Section 5.3 makes applicability limits clearer and the repository statement improves reproducibility documentation. These are useful but bounded gains. Unexplained fractional-count aggregation in new Table 2 and inconsistent Claude model labels in Table 1 limit the added evidence; the core results and appendices remain unchanged.
